# kite

> kite is a single-binary, dependency-free Kafka CLI (under 640 KB, written in Zig) that produces stdin lines to a topic and consumes a topic to stdout. It is built for scripts, containers, CI, and AI agents: no JVM, no librdkafka, no daemon, no prompts, and piped reads terminate on idle by default.

Repository: https://github.com/addisonhuddy/kite
License: Apache-2.0
Platforms: Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64
Brokers: any Kafka-protocol broker (Apache Kafka, Confluent Cloud, Redpanda, Amazon MSK with SASL/SCRAM, Aiven, WarpStream)
Security: PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL_SSL, SASL_PLAINTEXT; SASL PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512
Scope: produce and consume only. kite does not create topics, join consumer groups, commit offsets, or administer clusters.

## Install

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/addisonhuddy/kite/main/install.sh | sh
Options: --bin-dir DIR (or KITE_BIN_DIR), --version vX.Y.Z (or KITE_VERSION). Release checksums (SHA256SUMS) are verified.
From source: zig build (Zig 0.16.x).

## Configure

Precedence: flags > environment > properties file.
-b HOST:PORT[,HOST:PORT]        brokers
BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS               brokers
SECURITY_PROTOCOL               PLAINTEXT | SSL | SASL_SSL | SASL_PLAINTEXT
SASL_MECHANISM                  PLAIN | SCRAM-SHA-256 | SCRAM-SHA-512
SASL_USERNAME, SASL_PASSWORD
SSL_TRUSTSTORE_LOCATION         optional PEM CA bundle
--config FILE                   config file (also $KAFKA_PROPERTIES, ./kite.yaml, ./kite.properties, ~/.config/kite/)
--target NAME, @NAME            named cluster from kite.yaml's `clusters:` (also $KITE_TARGET or the file's `default:`)
kite --targets [--json]         list clusters in kite.yaml, `*` marks the selected one; reads only cluster names, never connects
kite --show-config --json       print effective config with provenance; never connects

## Produce (default mode)

kite [OPTIONS] TOPIC            one stdin line = one record
  value                         plain value
  key<TAB>value                 keyed record
  key<TAB>name: v<TAB>value     with headers
--json                          {"key":...,"value":...,"headers":{...}} per line; non-string value sent verbatim
--csv [--key COL]               RFC 4180 CSV rows -> JSON object values, optional key column
-H 'name: value'                header on every record (repeatable)
Produce is batched and idempotent by default. stdout is never written.

## Consume

kite -c [OPTIONS] TOPIC         records on stdout
-B, --from-beginning            earliest offset (default: latest)
--offset N  --partition P       start offset / single partition
-n, --max N                     stop after N records
-t, --idle DUR                  stop after DUR without records (3s, 500ms, 1m)
-f, --follow                    never stop on idle
--json                          {"topic","partition","offset","timestamp","key","headers","value"} per line
Default when stdout is a pipe or file: stop after 5 s idle, so scripts never hang.

## Contract

stdout: data only. stderr: diagnostics and end-of-run summary.
Exit 0 success; 1 any error with one line "kite: MESSAGE"; 130 on Ctrl-C.
No interactive prompts. No color unless a TTY (NO_COLOR / KITE_COLOR honored). No files written.
-q suppresses summaries; -v adds connection/retry diagnostics; KITE_DEBUG=1 adds frame/TLS traces.

## Examples

printf 'hello\n' | kite -b localhost:9092 events
kite -c -B -n 100 --idle 3s events
kite -c -B --json events | jq -c .value
kite -c -B --json src | kite --json dst
kite --csv --key user_id events < users.csv
tail -f app.log | kite logs
